recipes.name: Easy Turkey Taco Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 ounce) package frozen mixed vegetables (peas, carrots, green beans, corn)
2 (10 ounce) cans diced tomatoes with green chile peppers
1 (15 ounce) can ranch style chili beans

steps.text: Heat a large pot over medium-high heat and stir in the ground turkey and onion. Cook and stir until the turkey is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease. Add the mixed vegetables, tomatoes with green chiles, ranch beans, chicken broth, taco seasoning, and ranch dressing mix. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer on low for 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Turkey Taco Soup
raw_recipe.description: Ground turkey is a tasty alternative to the typical ground beef in other taco soups. The best part? This quick and easy soup needs only 30 minutes to simmer.

review.reviewBody: Very easy and tasty. We made it with some fresh veggies instead of frozen so the prep time was lengthened. Original recipe said 4 servings. They must be HUGE! I filled a large saucepan and didn't even use 2 10-ounce cans of tomatoes.

When I got this recipe in my inbox the day before Thanksgiving, I thought, "Perfect, I know what to do with the leftover turkey." A couple of days later, at the grocery store, I looked at the ingredients list. 
Needless to say, I went with 1 lb. of leftover turkey instead. I also made it in the slow cooker on low for about 5 hours. All of the other ingredients were per the recipe. And, it's a great soup. Good flavor and hearty. Would definitely make again.

I definitely made changes! Black beans instead of ranch style beans. Eliminated the ranch dressing mix. One can of rotel style tomatoes instead of two. Add one can diced tomatoes with garlic. One whole onion instead of 1/2 cup. That lowered the sodium content to about 260mg per serving, and lowered the carbs considerably!! AND it is so yummy!!

If the amount of sodium is too much, use low or no sodium broth, use fresh tomatoes or low sodium canned tomatoes. You can season the same as you do your chili. Chili powder, cumin etc. you can salt it to your taste rather than tear down the recipe provider.

I slightly altered this recipe as my DH can not tolerate hot-spicy. I used one can of tomatoes/peppers with two cartons chick broth. One can of corn, one can of beans, drained & rinsed with one packet of taco seasoning and one .4 oz pack of ranch mix with 2 cups diced pre-cooked chicken. I also sautéed the 1/2 cup diced onion. We enjoyed this soup and it took about 20 minutes to prepare.

I had 10 ounces of ground turkey that had been in the freezer for too long, and it was time to use it up, so I basically made about half this recipe. I used the full 1/2 cup of chopped onions, an entire 10 oz. bag of mixed veggies, one can of Rotel, an entire can of chili beans, the broth, and the taco and ranch mixes. I sautéed the onions in a little EVOO and added a couple of cloves of minced garlic during the last minute of sauteeing. Even though I’m not a huge fan of ground turkey, this turned out quite well. My version yielded 6 cups of soup.

I will make this again. I used 1 bag frozen C& W ultimate southwest blend of corn, black beans, poblano chilies, peppers and roasted onions, 2 cans of Rotel (with chilies and lime), 1 can Bush's southwestern pinto beans and all the rest of the mentioned recipe's ingredients (without the broth; I had enough turkey and chicken broth from the our Turkey Dinner). I even included the ranch dressing mix... which I wasn't sure I wanted to do! It looks good, smells wonderful and I'm pleased with the results!

Made this for our stay outta the rain soup. This was so easy. I don't vary from receipts but I did not have a few things on hand. No ranch beans (used kidney beans and a couple shakes of ranch dressing) left out green beans and give it extra corn, and cubed left over turkey and added it last cause it was all ready cooked. The flavor was awesome. My husband did not even doctor it with his jalapeño. I topped our dishes with chopped fresh scallions and mixed Mexican cheese. Microwaved 30 seconds to melt cheese and the Fritos corn chips on the side. This is going to be our winter soup for sure. This soup is 297 calories per cup. Carbs and sodium high.

My new go to recipe! Everyone loves this soup!! I used lean ground beef instead of turkey and did not drain the little bit of grease left it for flavor. I served this soup in a bowl over tortilla chips and topped with onions, jalapeños and grated 3 blend Mexican cheese and a dollop of sour cream. Yum yum!!

I did use low sodium chicken broth and taco seasoning. I didn't use a frozen bag of veggies. It added a can of whole kernel corn and garlic. I did use two cans of diced tomatoes. But so also added a small can of diced green chilis. Topped off with Mexican cheese blend, sour cream, cilantro, and fresh jalapeños. The flavor was so good!!! I have been perfecting this soup. To make it healthier, I'm using 96/4 turkey. I am also using chicken bone broth. Instead of chips or tortillas, I have added Avacado and jalapeños. This recipe keeps getting better. Oh, try the Southwest Ranch packet.....trust me.

Spicy, but not too spicy. I substituted ranch style beans with black beans and used leftover Thanksgiving turkey. Topped it with Mexican style cheese blend and sour cream. After all tacos are great with cheese and sour cream.

I use 2 15 oz cans of hotel diced tomatoes and green chili…also 4 small cans of tomato sauce, and two 10 oz bags of mixed vegetables. Turns it spicy and my family loves it…I eat it with cornbread on occasion. 😊😁

Well. I did not have leftover Turkey so I used ground Turkey. This recipe was so easy to follow and easy to make with big flavors. I did not use ranch seasoning because I did not have it. Italian green beans subbed for mixed veg. This was great. Served over garlic mashed potatoes.
Since I don't like spicy hot food, I used one can of tomatoes with chili peppers, no taco seasoning, and Pinto beans. I added enough chicken broth to make my desired thickness. It was very tasty.
I made w/leftover turkey, corn & green beans from Thanksgiving dinner. Just shredded turkey. Very good. Great way to use leftovers. Thanks. Debbie
Used leftover turkey instead of ground and will definitely make again. Next time would just use corn instead of the mixed veggies, but only because of my husband’s dislike of vegetables.
